Et iterum ait: Tollatur, ut non videat gloriam Domini, et cum hee facta fuerint, elongabit, inquit, Deus homines, et derelicti multiplicabuntur in terra. Ecce venient filit tui quos emisisti, venient collecti ab Oriente usque ad Occidentem verbo illius sancti, gaudentes ea que a Deo tuo est claritate. Exuere Hierusalem habitum luctus et afflictionis tue, et induere decorem ejus que a Deo tuo est claritatis in awternum: circumdare amictum duplicem ejus que a Deo tuo est justitie, impone mitram super caput tuum glorie eterne. Deus enim demonstrabit ei quae sub colo est universe tuum fulgorem. Vocabitur namque nomen tuum ab ipso Deo in weternum, pax justitice et glorie colenti Deo. Surge Hierusalem, et sta in excelso, et circumspice ad Orientem, et vide collectos filios tuos a Solis ortu usque ad Occidentem verbo illius sancti, gaudentes ipsam Dei recordationem. Profecti sunt enim a@ pedites, dum adducerentur ab inimicis. Introducet illos Deus ad te portatus cum gloria tanquam thronus regni. Et Apostolus autem scribens ad Galatas similiter ait: J//a autem que surswm est Hierusalem libera est, que est mater omnium nostrum ; non ex cogitatione erratici AXonis dicens hoc, neque virtute aliqua, que abscessit Pleromate, et Prunico; sed de Hierusalem quee in manibus descripta est. Et ipsam descendentem in Apocalypsi vidit Johannes super terram, novam. Post enim Regni tempora, Vidi, inquit, thronum album magnum, et sedentem in eo, cujus a facie fugit terra et colum, et locus non est eis. Et illa jam quee sunt generalis resurrectionis et judicii exponit vidisse, dicens mortuos magnos et minores. Dedit, inquit, > mare mortuos quos in se habuit, et mors et infert dederunt mortuos quos apud se habuerunt: et libri adaperti sunt. Et post heee ait: Vidi calum nowwm et terram novam: Primum enim calum et terra abierunt, etiam mare non est. Et audivi, inquit, vocem magnam de throno dicentem: Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis, et ipsi populi ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit corum Deus. Et delebit omnem lacrymam ab oculis eorum, et mors non erit amplius, non luctus non clamor neque dolor ulterius erit, quia prima abierunt. Et Esaias autem hoe ipsum ait: Erit enim obveniet eis in cor; sed latitiam et exultationem invenient in ea. autem est quod ab Apostolo dictum est: Preterit enim habitus hujus mundi. Similiter autem et Dominus ait: Terra et celum transiet. ~His itaque preetereuntibus super terram, novam superiorem Hierusalem ait Domini discipulus Johannes dere, quemadmodum sponsam ornatam viro suo; et hoe esse tabernaculum Dei, in quo inhabitabit Deus cum hominibus, HujusHierusalem imago illa, que in priori terra Hierusalem, in qua Sjusti preemeditantur incorruptelam, et parantur in salutem, Et hujus tabernaculi typum accepit Moyses in monte: et nihil allegorisari potest, sed omnia firma et vera, et substantiam habentia, ad fruitionem hominum justorum a Deo facta. Quomodo enim vere Deus est, qui resuscitat hominem; sic et vere resurgit a mortuis, et non allegorice, quemadmodum per tanta ostendimus.* Et sicut vere resurgit, sic et vere praemeditabitur ineorruptelam, et augebitur, et vigebit in regni temporibus, ut fiat CapaX glorize Patris. Deinde omnibus renovatis, vere in civitate habitabit Dei. Diwit, enim inquit, sedens super thronum: Ecce nova facio omnia. Et dicit Dominus; Omnia scribe, quomodo tt sermones fideles, et veri sunt. Et divit mihi, Facta sunt. Et secundum rationem.
thought_title: The Resurrection and the New Jerusalem
pass_a_gloss: But if certain ones have attempted to allegorize these things of this kind, they will not be able to be found consonant with themselves in all things, and they will be convinced by the very words themselves, because when the cities of the nations will have been deserted, and the houses, because they will not be inhabited, and the earth will be left deserted; For behold, Isaiah says, the day of the Lord is coming, incurable and full of fury and anger, to put the city on the earth deserted, and to destroy sinners from it. And again he says: Let him be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord, and when these things have been done, God will prolong, he says, the days of men, and the deserted ones will be multiplied on the earth. And they will build houses, and they themselves will inhabit, and they will plant vineyards, and they themselves will eat. These things have been spoken without controversy concerning the resurrection of the just, which occurs after the coming of the Antichrist and the destruction of all the nations that exist under him, in which the just will reign on the earth, growing from the vision of the Lord, and through him they will become accustomed to taking the glory of God, and the unity of spiritual things in the kingdom they will take. And those whom he finds on the earth, waiting for him from heaven, and having endured tribulation, who also escaped the hands of the wicked. These are the ones about whom the prophet says: And the deserted ones will be multiplied on the earth. And as many as of the believers God has prepared for this, to be deserted on the earth, and to be under the Kingdom of the Saints, and to minister to this Jerusalem, and the kingdom in it, Jeremiah the prophet signified, saying: Look around, he says, to the East, Jerusalem, and the joy that comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you sent out will come, coming gathered from the East to the West by the word of that holy one, rejoicing in the things that are from your God, with clarity. Put off, Jerusalem, the garment of mourning and your affliction, and put on the ornament of that which is from your God, with clarity, forever. Encircle yourself with a double garment of that which is from your God, of justice, and put a mitre on your head, of eternal glory. For God will show to her what is under the whole heaven, your splendor. For your name will be called by God himself, forever, peace of justice and glory, worshiping God. Arise, Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look around to the East, and see your sons gathered from the rising of the sun to the West, by the word of that holy one, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they have gone out on foot, while they were being led by enemies. God will introduce them to you, carried with glory, like a throne of the kingdom. For God has decreed that every high mountain will be humbled, and the eternal gatherings, and that the valleys will be filled, to reduce the plain of the earth, so that Israel may walk securely in the glory of God. And the trees have overshadowed the sycamores, and the wood of good odor, by the command of God, for Israel. For God will prohibit with joy, with the light of his clarity, with mercy and justice, which are from him. But all these things cannot be understood in the supercelestial things; for God, he says, will show to her what is under the heaven, your splendor; but in the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been recalled by Christ, and Jerusalem has been rebuilt, according to the character that is above, of Jerusalem, about which the prophet Isaiah says: Behold, I have depicted your walls in my hands, and you are always in my sight. And the Apostle, writing to the Galatians, says similarly: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is the mother of us all; not from the thought of the erratic Axe, saying this, nor by any virtue that has gone out from the Pleroma, and the Prunic; but from the Jerusalem that has been described in the hands. And John saw it descending on the earth, new, in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, I saw, he says, a great white throne, and one sitting on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled, and there was no place for them. And he explains the things that are of the general resurrection and judgment, saying: The sea gave up the dead that it had, and death and hell gave up the dead that they had; and the books were opened. And the book of life was opened, and the dead were judged from the things that were written in the books, according to their works; and death and hell were cast into the lake of fire, into the second death. This is what is called Gehenna, which the Lord said is eternal fire. And if anyone, he says, has not been found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire. And after these things, he says: I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and there is no longer any sea. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, descending from heaven, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard, he says, a great voice from the throne, saying: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them, their God. And he will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death, no more mourning, no more crying, no more pain, because the former things have passed away. And Isaiah says the same thing: For it will be a joy and an exultation that will come to them in their heart; but they will find gladness and exultation in it. This is what has been said by the Apostle: For the fashion of this world is passing away. Similarly, the Lord says: The earth and the heaven will pass away. When these things, therefore, are passing away, the Lord's disciple John says that there will be a new and superior Jerusalem on the earth, like a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God, in which God will dwell with men. And the image of this Jerusalem is that which is in the former earth, in Jerusalem, in which the just are prepared for incorruption, and are prepared for salvation. And Moses received the type of this tabernacle on the mountain; and nothing can be allegorized, but all things are firm and true, and have substance, made by God for the enjoyment of just men. For just as God is truly, who raises man; so also truly does he rise from the dead, and not allegorically, as we show through so many things. And just as he truly rises, so also will he truly prepare incorruption, and will increase, and will flourish in the times of the kingdom, so that he may become the perfect glory of the Father. Then, when all things have been renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For he says, sitting on the throne: Behold, I make all things new. And the Lord says: Write all things, how my words are faithful and true. And he says to me: They have been made. And according to reason.

pass_b_english:
If some attempt to allegorize these matters, they will not be found consistent with themselves in every respect, for the very words themselves will convict them. When the cities of the nations are deserted, when houses stand empty because no one lives in them, and the earth is left desolate, Isaiah declares: "Behold, the day of the Lord is coming, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make the land a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it" (Isaiah 13:9). He says again: "Let him be taken away, that he may not see the glory of the Lord" (Isaiah 13:19), and when these things have come to pass, God will prolong the days of men, and the deserted ones will multiply on the earth. They will build houses and inhabit them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit. These words speak plainly of the resurrection of the just, which takes place after the coming of the Antichrist and the destruction of all the nations that exist under his rule. In that time the just will reign on the earth, growing through the vision of the Lord and becoming accustomed through him to receive the glory of God and the unity of spiritual things in the kingdom. Those whom Christ finds on the earth, waiting for him from heaven and having endured tribulation, who also escaped the hands of the wicked — these are the ones of whom the prophet says, "And the deserted ones will be multiplied on the earth." As many believers as God has prepared for this, to be left on the earth and to serve under the Kingdom of the Saints, ministering to this Jerusalem and the kingdom within it, Jeremiah the prophet foretold, saying: "Look around toward the east, O Jerusalem, and see the joy that comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you sent away shall come, gathered from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of your God. Put off the garment of your mourning and affliction, O Jerusalem, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from your God. Wrap yourself in the robe of righteousness from your God; place on your head the crown of eternal glory. For God will show your splendor to all under heaven. Your name shall be called by God forever: peace of righteousness and glory to those who worship God. Arise, O Jerusalem, stand on the height; look toward the east and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them. For they went out on foot, led away by enemies; but God will bring them back to you, carried in glory as upon a royal throne. For God has decreed that every high mountain shall be made low, and the everlasting hills, and the valleys filled up, to make level ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God. The woods and every fragrant tree have shaded Israel at God's command. For God will lead Israel with joy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.

But these things cannot be understood as belonging to some supercelestial realm; for God says he will show Jerusalem's splendor to all under heaven — yet this happens in the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been reclaimed by Christ and Jerusalem rebuilt according to the pattern of the Jerusalem above, of which Isaiah says: "Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me." The Apostle writes to the Galatians in the same way: "But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother" (Galatians 4:26) — not from the thought of some errant Aeon, nor by any virtue that has emanated from the Pleroma and the Prunicus, but from the Jerusalem that has been depicted in the hands of God. And John saw this Jerusalem descending, new, upon the earth in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, he says: "Then I saw a great white throne and him who was seated on it. From his presence earth and sky fled away, and no place was found for them" (Revelation 20:11). He describes the general resurrection and judgment: "The sea gave up the dead who were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done. Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. And if anyone's name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire" (Revelation 20:13-15). This is what is called Gehenna, which the Lord said is eternal fire. And after these things John says: "Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away'" (Revelation 21:1-4). Isaiah says the same: "They shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away." This is what the Apostle declared: "The form of this world is passing away." So also the Lord says: "Heaven and earth will pass away." When these things therefore pass away on the earth, the Lord's disciple John says there will be a new and higher Jerusalem on the earth, like a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God, in which God will dwell with men. The image of this Jerusalem is the one that existed on the former earth, in Jerusalem, where the just are prepared for incorruption and made ready for salvation. Moses received the pattern of this tabernacle on the mountain; and nothing can be allegorized — all things are firm and true, possessing substance, made by God for the enjoyment of just men. For just as God is truly the One who raises man, so also he truly rises from the dead, and not allegorically, as we have shown through so many proofs. And just as he truly rises, so also will he truly prepare incorruption, and will increase, and will flourish in the times of the kingdom, that he may become the perfect glory of the Father. Then, when all things have been renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For the One seated on the throne says: "Behold, I make all things new." And the Lord says: "Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true." And he said to me: "It is done." And this is according to reason.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text, including the complex theological arguments regarding the literal vs. allegorical interpretation of the resurrection and the New Jerusalem. Scripture citations in Pass B (Isaiah 13:9, 13:19, Galatians 4:26, Revelation 20:11-15, Revelation 21:1-4) correctly identify the biblical passages alluded to in the Latin. Pass A is a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B is a fluent English version that preserves all nuances of agency and modality. No omissions or contradictions found.
